newsitem.title: UK: European cotton market sees selective buying.
newsitem.headline: European cotton market sees selective buying.

text.p: Europe's raw cotton markets saw a moderate level of fresh business at steady rates despite increased prices for finished yarn, industry sources said.
Additional lots of Central Asian styles were sold to customary Italian buyers and there were reports of new sales of selected upland description to North African spinners.
Several yarn producers said that increased yarn prices were not enough to offset the higher replacement cotton costs created by the strong U.S. dollar. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8071
